A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from Prefix-Tuning+ to PrefixMemory-Tuning. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated diagnostics and retained results.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, out-of-distribution generalization, representation-analysis, and preference-alignment experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds math-reasoning results, feature-map and LoRA-rank comparisons, and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The core external memory contribution remains unchanged: v1 Equation 8 becomes v3 Equation 7. V3 adds an evaluated GELU feature-map option to v1's ELU implementation. Trainable MLP maps were already contemplated in v1; their newly reported evaluation and the method's renaming do not establish a new architecture.

E1.justification: V3 adds WebInstruct-CFT training and open-ended math evaluation on AMC23, AIME24, and Minerva-Math, substantially extending coverage beyond classification and preference alignment. The original classification datasets, TruthfulQA representation diagnostic, and Magpie/UltraFeedback alignment evaluations remain.

E2.justification: LoRA+ becomes an evaluated comparator in both model blocks of Table 1; v1 cited it without reporting these comparisons. Existing full fine-tuning, LoRA, Prefix-Tuning, and in-context-learning comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include critique fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Math-7B with 4K, 10K, and 50K examples, LoRA rank sweeps at 32/16/8, and training-throughput and inference-latency evaluations, including a 72B model. The original few-shot sampling, 4,000 training steps, and batch size of two remain documented.

E4.justification: V3 adds feature-map comparisons covering ELU, GELU, and an MLP kernel (Table 2), LoRA rank and parameter-budget analyses (Appendix A.4), and computational-cost analyses (Section 6.3). These substantially extend the existing OOD, data-size, attention-pattern, spectrum, and CKA diagnostics, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging the few-shot experiments over five independent sampling rounds. V3 adds no seed specification, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance-testing procedure; its additional tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: The original classification, alignment, and CKA values are retained. V3 adds LoRA+, feature-map, rank, math, and efficiency results. For example, Table 3 reports 50K-example Minerva-Math accuracy of 62.5% for PMT versus 23.9% for LoRA. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over v1 under an existing setting.

T1.justification: V3 omits v1's explicit ICL definition and Equation 9 describing an optional normalized memory term kept inside attention. The central prefix decomposition, kernel construction, and appendix covariance/CKA mathematics remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central bottleneck diagnosis, external-prefix contribution, and claimed average few-shot advantages remain. V3's introduction and conclusion broaden the practical-utility claim to critique-based math reasoning and explicitly emphasize training and inference efficiency, while retaining the proof-of-concept framing.

C2.justification: V3 connects its design to prompt-memory capacity limits and adds discussion of trainable-map initialization and stability. Appendix E explicitly qualifies extrapolation from 3B–7B downstream evaluations to larger models; the 72B experiment measures latency. Most existing mechanism interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V3 documents a code-repository address, explicitly states feature-map and memory dimensions, and supplies parameter counts in Table 8. Appendix C's optimizer, DeepSpeed, precision, learning-rate, and GPU-count information is retained. The added math and timing experiments receive limited implementation detail.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to DePT, ADePT, E2VPT, feed-forward networks as memory, prompt interpretability, and test-time adaptation. V3 also relates its design to Meyer et al.'s memory limitations, distinguishes QLoRA from LoRA+ more accurately, and adds critique-fine-tuning and math references.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the paper and method, v3 substantially rewrites the introduction and related work, separates feature-map discussion, and reorganizes experiments into diagnostics, applications, and efficiency. Detailed setup moves to Appendix A.1, the original discussion becomes Appendix D, and a new conclusion and LLM-usage disclosure are added.

P2.justification: V3 adds an architecture diagram, six new tables, and LoRA+ columns in Table 1. The original attention map moves from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 10. Retained plots and tables are rearranged within a new conference layout, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the practical case through open-ended math evaluation, a stronger LoRA+ comparison, feature-map and parameter-budget controls, and measured computational costs—important evidence missing from v1's proof of concept. These gains outweigh documentation weaknesses: Table 2 reports MLP results while surrounding text leaves MLPs to future work, Appendix A.4 overstates a monotonic rank–accuracy trend, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. The improvement is primarily in empirical support and research positioning.
